event_context.day_index_convention: 0 = Opening Sunday (gate opens 12:01am). Negative = days before opening (Early Arrival / staging). 6 = Burn Saturday. 7 = Temple Sunday. 8 = Labor Day Monday. 9 = Tuesday after.
event_context.timezone: All hours are Pacific (playa time), 24h clock.

measures.gravel_to_gate: Official ingress metric: end of pavement/gravel on CR-34 to the Gate. This is what @bmantraffic reports.
measures.gate_road_to_gravel: Official Exodus metric: Greeters/Gate Road to the pavement of CR-34.
measures.cr34_8mile_to_gate: From the 8-mile playa entrance on County Route 34 to the gate (news phrasing).
measures.others: Personal/anecdotal measures (reno_to_camp, gate_line_personal) are NOT comparable to the official metric and are marked low confidence.

observations.quote: I also knew that there was only a 10 minute entrance line at 7AM Tues.
The early entry line last year was weird too. Same congestion...waited 3-4 hours on early Thursday.

Last year, we left Sacramento at 3:00PM on Sunday, and got to our campsite at 3:00AM ... it took ten hours to get from Reno to camp on opening day, almost all of that sitting in traffic the last 30 miles.
last year I got there 10:00 mon morn and had a 4 hour wait.

patterns.claim: Wait times during the first 36 hours after opening can be five or more hours.
If you can arrive Tuesday or later, you will find your wait time to be much shorter.
On all days but opening night, the shortest lines are usually in the early morning hours, generally from 3 a.m.-10 a.m.
Heavy traffic and longer wait times indeed happen Saturday, Sunday and Monday.
Gate Road travel times during Exodus peaked at six to nine hours just to get from Greeters to the pavement of County Road 34.
Allow up to 12 hours to reach the Reno airport during peak egress (Exodus).
Best exodus windows: try to leave very early in the morning, in the later evening, or on Tuesday morning before noon.
For 2026 Burning Man is aiming for a maximum ingress travel time - from the gravel to the Gate - of four hours whenever possible.
Waits of 6+ hours once you get to the playa are common at peak arrival hours (Sunday mid-day through Tuesday night, with ebbs and flows within that time period).
If you arrive from about Wednesday onwards, you're not going to have any real problems with entry lines.
Even if you have Early Entry passes you can still expect to wait half an hour to a couple hours at gate.
In 2014, some people waited upwards of 18 hours in line after the gate was closed due to rain.

Arriving before the 12:01am opening is actively punished: early arrivals without credentials are staged behind on-time drivers. In 2019, arriving at 11:49pm meant ~5 hours; arriving one minute later meant 25 minutes.
2023 was the mud-year anomaly: the driving ban meant Exodus, not ingress, was the extreme. Exodus ran 5h10m -> 6h -> 8h through Monday Sept 4 evening and was still ~7.5h Tuesday morning.
2024 opening was weather-shifted: the gate closed for rain and reopened around 3:15pm Saturday, roughly 12 hours after closure, with ~20,000 people waiting.

2025 was the worst modern ingress year in this dataset: an Aug 23 windstorm (45-50+ mph gusts) closed the gate, and the backlog produced 6-9 hour official waits through Monday Aug 25 and into Tuesday Aug 26.
Reported wait is self-defeating: when the reported Gate Road travel time is low, many folks choose that moment to leave, which can increase those times faster than they can be reported.
More than one third of Burners arrive on the first Monday of the event; a quarter still arrive after Monday, peaking again on the Thursday.
Early Arrival (work access) holders are ~12% of the population and enter before 6pm Sunday; in 2018 the Early-Arrival-only line still ran 2-4 hours on the Thursday/Friday/Saturday before opening.

Averaged over 2014-2017, ingress wait peaks roughly 18-26 hours after the gate opens (Sunday evening into Monday pre-dawn) at about 5 hours, is near zero in the first 2-4 hours after opening, and shows a second smaller ~2.5h bump around 58-62 hours after opening.
Averaged over 2014-2017, Exodus wait is low until the Temple burn (~24h after Man burn), then rises to a 3-4 hour plateau across the following 12-36 hours.
2024 ingress collapsed to a flat 20-minute floor from event Wednesday onward and never exceeded 30 minutes from Thursday to Burn Saturday.
2025 ingress stayed at or above 6 hours from Opening Sunday 09:00 through Tuesday 06:00 almost continuously, peaking at 8h40m on Monday 10:00.
Exodus peaks Sunday night (Temple Sunday ~20:00-23:00) and again Monday evening; the Tuesday-after window collapses to ~25-45 minutes.
BMIR 94.5 / GARS 95.1 FM broadcast hourly Gate Road wait reports at the top of the hour; @bmantraffic posts the same numbers, which is why hourly series exist at all.

notes:
PROVENANCE. The 2024 and 2025 hourly series are the backbone of this dataset. They come from bmantravel.com's data.js, which is a community aggregation of the hourly @bmantraffic reports (396 readings). I verified that aggregation against 8 primary @bmantraffic tweets whose exact Pacific timestamps I decoded from their Twitter snowflake IDs; every one matched the aggregated value for that date+hour exactly (e.g. 2025-08-25 15:00 -> 480 min vs tweet 'travel time from Gravel to Gate is 8 hours'). Those 8 tweets are also included as separate rows with source_type 'official'.

HARD DATA vs GUIDANCE. 'observations' and 'exodus' contain only figures a source actually stated (or, for source_type 'chart', values read off a published plot and explicitly marked low confidence with +/-0.5h axis precision). Advice like 'arrive Tuesday' lives in 'patterns' and is never mixed into the numeric rows.

CONFIDENCE LADDER. high = official @bmantraffic / burningman.org / the verified hourly aggregation, or a news outlet quoting an official figure. medium = news or a well-sourced community write-up. low = a single anecdote, or a value read off a chart.

KNOWN GAPS. There is no hour-level series for 2017-2023. I located the raw material for 2018 (255 archived tweets), 2019 (116), 2022 (303) and 2023 (77) in the Wayback Machine under twitter.com/bmantraffic/status/*, and confirmed the method works (the tweet text sits in the archived page's <title>, and the exact Pacific timestamp is recoverable from the tweet ID). web.archive.org rate-limited and then IP-blocked this host partway through the harvest, so only a handful of 2018/2019 rows landed. Re-running the harvest from a fresh IP with ~2s pacing would fill 2018, 2019, 2022 and 2023 to the same hour-level fidelity as 2024/2025. See scratchpad files fetchlist.txt / batch_prio.txt for the exact URL list.

OTHER DEAD ENDS. reddit.com is blocked at both the tool and network level here (403 on www/old/api/.json and on redlib mirrors), eplaya.burningman.org 403s direct requests (Wayback was the only route in), Facebook groups are login-walled, and Burning Man's own open-data portal (innovate.burningman.org) publishes no traffic or gate dataset.

CAVEAT ON COMPARABILITY. The gate opening time itself changed over the period: it moved earlier in 2014 (8 hours earlier than 2013, 14 hours earlier than historically), so 'hours after gate opens' curves from 2014-2017 are not directly comparable to a 2024/2025 clock-time series. Also, 2023 (mud), 2024 (rain, 12-hour gate closure) and 2025 (45-50mph windstorm closure) were all weather-disrupted years; none of the last three years is a clean baseline.
